name: Dark Iron dwarf
summary: Beneath Blackrock Mountain, Dark Iron dwarves live under Ragnaros's rule. Banished from Ironforge after the War of the Three Hammers, they have built a society shaped by fire and tyranny.

sections.title: Fiery Heritage and Exile
sections.body:
Dark Iron dwarves have dark gray or soot-black skin and eyes like glowing embers. Their Bronzebeard and Wildhammer cousins look different. Their people split during the War of the Three Hammers, when Sorcerer-thane Thaurissan tried to conquer Ironforge. Defeated, he led them south into the Redridge Mountains.

There, he sought dark powers to avenge his losses and released Ragnaros the Firelord from the Elemental Plane. The summoning shattered the surrounding peaks into the volcanic waste of Blackrock Mountain. It bound the Dark Iron to fiery servitude.

sections.title: Under the Firelord's Shadow
sections.body:
Life in Shadowforge, deep beneath the mountain, is brutal. The Dark Irons were once ambitious and cunning, but generations beneath Ragnaros's oppressive aura have warped much of their culture. Cruelty, paranoia, and tyranny now shape it.

Dark Iron law gives one sentence for infractions: trial by combat in the Ring of the Law. Poisoning and political intrigue run so deep that Dark Iron travelers bring their own rations rather than trust food from strangers.

sections.title: Splinters and Outcasts
sections.body:
Not all Dark Iron dwarves serve Emperor Dagran Thaurissan and the cult of Ragnaros. Dissident factions have broken away to follow their own ends. The best known is the Thorium Brotherhood, a guild of master smiths based at Thorium Point in Searing Gorge. They left the main clan and hire outsiders to fight their former masters.

Other Dark Irons work as mercenaries, spies, or trade engineers alongside neutral groups such as the Venture Company.

faq.q: Why do Dark Iron dwarves have gray skin and red eyes?
aliases: why do dark irons look like that
faq.answer: Dark gray skin and fiery red eyes are natural traits that distinguish Dark Iron dwarves from mountain and hill dwarves. Life deep underground near the mountain's elemental fires has further marked their volcanic nature.

faq.q: Are all Dark Iron dwarves evil?
faq.answer: No. Imperial Dark Iron society is treacherous. The legendary architect Franclorn Forgewright and the rebel smiths who broke from the clan show honor, valor, and independence from its corruption.

faq.q: Where is the capital of the Dark Iron dwarves?
faq.answer: Dark Iron civilization centers on Shadowforge City, deep in the subterranean caverns of Blackrock Depths within Blackrock Mountain. Their emperor rules from there.

faq.q: What is the Ring of the Law?
faq.answer: The Ring of the Law is the arena where Dark Iron justice is carried out. Crimes against the clan carry the death penalty, and the accused must pay the blood price by fighting waves of vicious beasts and gladiators. Virtually no prisoner survives.

The Thorium Brotherhood is a rogue faction of Dark Iron craftsmen who broke away from the main clan. Based at Thorium Point in Searing Gorge, they trade their unmatched knowledge of fiery metallurgy and Dark Iron smithing secrets to outsiders willing to undermine the imperial clan.

angles.text: For Bronzebeard dwarves of Ironforge, the Dark Irons are a family feud turned existential threat, rooted in their bloody rebellion during the War of the Three Hammers.
Dark Iron artisans are renowned smiths with exclusive mastery of Dark Iron ore. It takes the searing heat of Blackrock Mountain's Black Forge to melt and shape it.
Alliance scouts watch the Dark Irons warily. Their imperial armies are an aggressive, expansionist menace pressing against Ironforge's southern borders.
The Horde sees the Dark Irons as dangerous zealots occupying Blackrock Mountain and threatening Horde supply routes through the Badlands and nearby passes.
